title: Enterprise reserved pool concierge: SLA negotiation and scaling rubric
creator: Aisha Romero
body:
Summary:
This ticket captures a standardized rubric and concierge workflow for negotiating enterprise reserved GPU pools. The goal is to provide consistent guidance when customers request SLA-backed reserved throughput: target p95 latency and throughput guarantees, preferred GPU families, burst/oversubscription policies, preemption tolerances, and operational observability expectations.

Problem & motivation:
Enterprise customers are requesting bespoke reserved capacity with explicit SLAs (throughput and latency guarantees) and preferences for GPU classes. Currently intake is ad hoc, causing long negotiation cycles and inconsistent commitments from Eng/Capacity teams. We need an intake rubric that balances engineering risk, cost, and customer value, and produces a clear deliverable: a committed pool profile (size, GPU family, scaling policy, fallback model variants, pricing delta, and runbook).

Scope:
- Non-bug feature triage for dedicated/reserved requests only (not hosted pay-as-you-go).
- End-to-end concierge workflow: intake form, triage rubric, engineering sizing guidance, required console changes (UI to show reserved pool assignments), contract checklist for legal/Security, and SRE runbook for escalation.
- Deliverables: a 1-page rubric, intake questionnaire template, sizing checklist, and an example negotiation artifact for a reference customer.

Key decision areas (rubric components):
1) SLA target & KPIs: p95 latency goal (ms), min sustained throughput (tokens/s or rps), availability SLO (%, monthly uptime), and burst envelope (short lived above commit).
2) GPU family options: recommend tiers (cost vs performance): Tiers are (A) Hopper-class (H100/next-gen): best latency/throughput for dense transformer models, (B) Ampere-class (A100): balanced, (C) Efficient-quantized CPU / L4-class for lower-cost inference. Provide recommended fallbacks.
3) Reserved capacity sizing: use 3 inputs: expected sustained qps, peak qps, and typical sequence length distribution. Provide quick-sizing rules-of-thumb and link to sizing spreadsheet.
4) Scaling policy & burst behavior: define autoscale headroom, burst credits, pre-warm windows, and hard caps. Decide on proactive vs. reactive scaling based on customer SLAs.
5) Preemption & availability: whether work can tolerate preemptible VMs/GPU reclaim; if not, reserve non-preemptible pool at premium pricing.
6) Isolation & data-flow: whether customer requires dedicated tenancy (VPC/private) or just reserved multi-tenant pools with data separation.
7) Observability & alerts: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency p50/ p95, capacity utilization dashboards and SLO burn rate alerts.
8) Rollout and fallbacks: enforce canary policies, automatic fallback to compatible model variant (smaller model or quantized) when pool is strained.

Acceptance criteria:
- A filled rubric template can convert a customer request into a deterministic set of deliverables: GPU family, pool size, SLA targets, cost delta, and runbook.
- Console changes (UX story) documented and prioritized in a follow-up ENG ticket.
- Pricing sheet updated with reserved rates for each GPU tier and burst policy.
- Legal and security checklist documented and sign-off flow captured.

Notes from initial triage meeting (2025-03-06):
- Customer A use-case: high-frequency chat routing (avg seq 256 tokens), wants 99.9% availability, p95 latency <120ms, sustain 1800 rps, peak 2500 rps for 30s bursts. Recommended preliminary: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs with burst headroom, canary rollout over 48h, non-preemptible pool.
- Engineering feedback: we need telemetry for model-mapped utilization and per-route batching efficiency before committing to >8 GPUs. Mark ENG-7521 to add these telemetry hooks.
- Security: VPC requirement will push this into Private deployment SKU; coordinate with Security for KMS and audit retention. DES-204 to validate console display patterns for reserved pools.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Price vs latency: Do we standardize three pricing tiers or negotiate per-customer? Recommendation: baseline standard tiers, but permit negotiated add-ons for custom SLAs.
- Burst policy: Should burst credit be purchased up-front (prepaid buffer) or billed usage-based? Preference towards prepaid for predictability.
- Model fallbacks: Can we enforce automatic model fallback in the platform when pool under pressure? This requires runtime integration and risk of quality regressions. Mark as medium-risk engineering effort (ENG-8110).

Risks & mitigations:
- Overcommit risk: committing fixed GPUs without utilization signal. Mitigate by requiring usage telemetry and conservative initial sizing + 30-day review.
- Quality regressions if fallback models are used: require customer acceptance testing and evals hooked to release pipeline.
- Legal/Security delays: surface requirements during intake and flag for early engagement.

Next steps (owners):
- PM (Diego): finalize rubric doc and intake questionnaire (due 2025-03-14).
- Eng (Sana Patel, ENG-7521): add per-pool telemetry hooks and a utilization dashboard (estimate 5 points, due 2025-03-28).
- Eng (Runtime team, ENG-8110): prototype automatic model fallback behavior and failure modes (spike testing).
- Design (DES-204): wireframes for console reserved pool assignment and SLA summary panel (due 2025-03-18).
- Legal & Security: sign-off checklist to be added to intake template; security review requested for all non-standard pools.

Links & artifacts:
- Sizing spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/enterprise-reserved-sizing (internal)
- Draft rubric doc (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Reserved+Pool+Rubric
- Telemetry PR (stub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5821

Definition of done:
- Rubric and intake template published in Confluence, onboarding doc for Solutions Engineers updated, and a follow-up ENG ticket(s) created for console and runtime work (linked in dependencies).

Stakeholders to notify on completion: Solutions Engineering, Sales AE, Legal, Security, Runtime Eng, Console UX.
